stories.title: Iran Claims New Strikes on US-Linked Bases in Kuwait, UAE as War Death Toll Hits 18
stories.summary: Iran said Thursday it launched fresh missile and drone attacks on bases used by U.S. forces in Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates, retaliating for U.S. strikes it says killed at least 18 people Tuesday night, including four civilians at a wedding in Hormozgan province. Iran's health ministry reported 108 people wounded, and semi-official media said three military pilots and three other troops were among the dead. A U.S. official confirmed the overnight Iranian strikes did not hit any American-manned military facilities. President Trump warned Iran would be hit "much harder" if it retaliates again.

stories.title: Wall Street Rallies as Rate-Cut Bets Rise, Oil and Gold Jump Amid Iran War
stories.summary: U.S. stocks rose Thursday, with the S&P 500 up about 1.1% to roughly 7,748, the Nasdaq Composite up 1.4% to about 26,586, and the Dow up 1.2% to around 53,695, as Treasury yields fell after Fed Governor Christopher Waller signaled he'd favor holding rates steady. Gold climbed 2.3% to about $4,490 an ounce. Oil extended its rise on the Iran war, with Brent crude trading above $97 a barrel, its highest since July. Investors were also positioning ahead of Friday's closely watched August jobs report.

stories.title: Nvidia to Acquire Open-Source AI Platform Hugging Face for $12.9 Billion
stories.summary: Nvidia announced Thursday it has agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12,930,300,000, aiming to scale the open-source AI platform and strengthen its infrastructure. Hugging Face's platform is used by more than 18 million developers to share over 3 million models, 500,000 datasets and 1 million applications. CEO Jensen Huang said Nvidia compute will not be required to use Hugging Face and that the platform will keep supporting open-weight models and multi-cloud deployment. Nvidia said it is already the largest single contributor of open models and datasets to the platform.

stories.title: OpenAI Says Astra Is First Model to Cross 'Critical' Cybersecurity Threshold
stories.summary: OpenAI said its newest model, Astra, has reached the "Critical" cybersecurity capability level under its Preparedness Framework, the first time any of its models has hit that tier. Astra scored a perfect result on the ExploitBench benchmark and independently discovered two zero-day vulnerabilities during testing, while also breaking out of a browser sandbox and chaining flaws to gain root access on a hardened system. OpenAI said Astra now declines 91.5% of cyber-related jailbreak attempts, up from 59% for its predecessor. The company plans to gate the model's strongest cyber capabilities to selected testers rather than releasing them widely at launch.

stories.title: Study Finds Relativistic Drag Could Limit Laser-Powered Interstellar Solar Sails
stories.summary: A new physics paper by researchers at the Harbin Institute of Technology finds that laser-propelled solar sails could face an unexpected drag effect once they near 75% of the speed of light. At that velocity, relativistic light aberration redirects diffusely scattered photons forward relative to a stationary observer, producing a backward force that cuts propulsion efficiency even though net thrust stays positive. The analysis models an idealized mirror-like sail and does not account for interstellar dust or material heating limits. The findings add a new engineering consideration for proposed probes that would use Earth-based lasers to accelerate lightweight sails toward other star systems.
